column1: # Consumed by tests/host (C) and the Python reference model.
# Adding a case here is the ONLY sanctioned way to change rewrite behaviour:
# both consumers must agree, which is what stops the supervisor-side and
# "=" in expected means "unchanged, AND the implementation must return the
# input pointer itself, not a copy" (docs/04-preload-spec.md R1/§5.1). The
# harness asserts pointer identity for these rows, not just string equality --
# returning a copy is a silent per-call memcpy in the hot path.
# A literal string in expected means "must return a rewritten/normalized
# buffer". Note that a path needing normalization which then turns out to be a
# sysdir (e.g. /proc/./self/maps) returns the NORMALIZED string, not the input
# pointer -- so its expected column is the normalized form, never "=".
# "!TOOLONG" means the call must return NULL with err == ALR_E_TOOLONG.
# (hot path: git increasingly uses openat(dirfd, relative))
# --- component boundary: these are NOT sysdirs -----------------------------
# ...but a sibling that merely shares a string prefix is NOT under root
# --- dotdot clamps at the guest root, never escapes ------------------------
# THE most important block in this file. These pass only if alr_rw normalizes
# BEFORE the sysdir and already-under-root checks. Both of those are
# component-boundary prefix matches, so they fire on UNNORMALIZED input and
# return early -- with the wrong ordering the guest silently reads the ANDROID
# HOST's file instead of the rootfs's.
# Acceptance string: PRELOAD NORMALIZE BEFORE SYSDIR.
# same trick against the idempotency guard
# normalization happened, so the NORMALIZED buffer comes back even though the
# result is already under root -- not the input pointer. See the header note.
# ...and legitimate sysdir paths must still pass through after normalizing
# --- root with a trailing slash is normalised away by alr_trim_root --------
# --- empty root = passthrough mode (ALR_ROOT unset or invalid) --------------
# 4000-char guest path under a 16-char root overflows ALR_PBUF(4096).
# Generated by the harness (see GEN_TOOLONG), not spelled out here.
